en: Itivuttaka 98: Tikanipāta, Pañcamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a stone, the person who is like a water jar, and the person who is like a lotus. And how, monks, is a person like a stone? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hatred toward his mother, his father, his brothers, his sisters, his friends, his companions, his kinsmen, and his relatives; he dwells with a mind full of hatred toward ascetics and brahmins, and even toward the multitude of beings. This, monks, is called a person like a stone. And how, monks, is a person like a water jar? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind free from hatred toward his mother, his father, his brothers, his sisters, his friends, his companions, his kinsmen, and his relatives; he dwells with a mind free from hatred toward ascetics and brahmins, and even toward the multitude of beings. Yet, when others abuse him, revile him, scold him, or harass him, he becomes angry, resentful, and harbors ill will. This, monks, is called a person like a water jar. And how, monks, is a person like a lotus? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind free from hatred toward his mother, his father, his brothers, his sisters, his friends, his companions, his kinsmen, and his relatives; he dwells with a mind free from hatred toward ascetics and brahmins, and even toward the multitude of beings. And when others abuse him, revile him, scold him, or harass him, he does not become angry, resentful, or harbor ill will. This, monks, is called a person like a lotus. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the monks: "Friends, monks! "Yes, friend," those monks replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, the Blessed One has spoken of three kinds of persons. Of these, which one is the best? When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta replied to the Venerable Ānanda: "Friend Ānanda, of these three persons, the one who is like a lotus is the best. When this was said, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna replied to the Venerable Sāriputta: "Friend Sāriputta, of these three persons, the one who is like a water jar is the best. When this was said, the Venerable Mahākassapa replied to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: "Friend Moggallāna, of these three persons, the one who is like a stone is the best. When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the monks: "Friends, monks! "Yes, friend," those monks replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, the Blessed One has spoken of three kinds of persons. Of these, which one is the best? When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta replied to the Venerable Ānanda: "Friend Ānanda, of these three persons, the one who is like a lotus is the best. When this was said, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna replied to the Venerable Sāriputta: "Friend Sāriputta, of these three persons, the one who is like a water jar is the best. When this was said, the Venerable Mahākassapa replied to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: "Friend Moggallāna, of these three persons, the one who is like a stone is the best. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported all that had occurred. When this was said, the Blessed One told the Venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, among these three persons, the one who is like a stone is indeed the best. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, that person does not harbor malice toward anyone, nor does he give rise to ill will. Therefore, Ānanda, among these three persons, the one who is like a stone is indeed the best. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. The Discourse on Giving.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Monks, there are these two kinds of giving."
The gift of material goods and the gift of the Dhamma.
Of these two gifts, monks, the gift of the Dhamma is foremost.
There are, monks, these two kinds of sharing:

The sharing of material things and the sharing of the Dhamma. Of these two kinds of sharing, monks, the sharing of the Dhamma is the foremost. “Support with material goods and support with the Dhamma.
Of these two kinds of support, monks, the support with the Dhamma is the foremost.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
"That which they call the supreme, unsurpassed gift,
which the Blessed One praised as sharing."
Who that is wise and discerning would not, with a mind full of faith, offer sacrifice at the proper time in this most excellent field?
Both those who speak and those who hear— both these [should do so].
"For those whose minds are confident in the teaching of the Sugata,
and who are heedful in the teaching of the Sugata, their supreme goal becomes purified."
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The ninth [discourse].
